title: Seattle, Tuesday
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Seattle. A different rain. A gallery window. Wood is crying. It's the trying.

panels.composition: Seattle, drawn from a postcard and nerve: a steep hill of wet brick, buildings taller than any in the strip, rain that is somehow a different rain. WOOD and CHLOE under one umbrella.

image.prompt: a steep city hill of wet brick with tall buildings, two young people sharing one umbrella in a fine city rain, drawn from imagination, brush-pen black and white

panels.composition: A gallery window. Something made of light inside. Wood stopped in front of it.

balloons.text: Everything here is trying so hard.

image.prompt: a young man stopped in front of a gallery window glowing with an artwork made of light, a young woman beside him under an umbrella

panels.composition: Chloe, looking at him, not the window.

image.prompt: close-up of a young woman looking at a young man whose face is wet under an umbrella in front of a lit window

panels.composition: The two of them walking on up the hill, small, the umbrella, the city. The strip's most beautiful drawing of a place the author has never been.

image.prompt: two small figures under one umbrella walking up a steep wet city hill between tall buildings at dusk, drawn with more care than the town ever got, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox
